references.text: The immediately preceding verse describes that the flood was on the earth for 40 days and that the water lifted the ark from the ground.
Continues the description from verse 18 of how the water kept rising and covered all the high mountains under the sky.
Describes how God remembered Noah and caused the waters to recede, so that the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat - contrasting with the rising waters in 7:18.
The Lord reigns over the flood (mabbul) - the only other place in the Old Testament that uses the word mabbul, referring to God's sovereignty over the floodwaters.
A poetic description of how God covered the earth with water and set boundaries for it, reflecting the flood narrative.
Mentions Noah's faith as he built the ark to save his family from the flood, showing the spiritual dimension of the events in Genesis 7:18.
Direct narrative connection describing the beginning and development of the same flood event.
Complementary parts of the same account that together describe the duration and consequences of the flood.
A theological contrast between creation and the flood judgment, both demonstrating God's sovereignty over water and earth.
Complementary verses marking respectively the peak and the end of the flood period.
Direct narrative link confirming the total coverage of water on which the ark floated.
A clear allusion where the flood in the Psalm uses the historical event as a metaphor for God's salvation.
